_meta.purpose: Converging code lane: four grade rounds with blocking counts 3/2/1/1, recorded cap halt at the 4th re-entry of code-grade with max 3 under the counting-only guard. Under the whole-lap progress rule the improving laps 2-3 waive (re-entry 1 is always unknown-counting, lap 4 reads unchanged) so the cap never trips — the converging-loop waiver pinned on a real trail.
_meta.excerpt_rule: Trail lines 72-118 in verbatim order: every code-cite-check row, every code-grade unit row, the four code-snapshot and four code-fix rows (round delimiters — a different-channel stage row closes a round), all routing rows, and the halt row. Dropped within the range: the four code-demote stage rows (publish no channel, no fold reads them; their outgoing routing rows stay).
_meta.channel_rule: Each stage row bakes its outcome channel in `channel` (derived from the workflow's outcome map so the replay needs no workflow introspection): code-cite-check->code-cite-check; code-grade/code-confirm->code-verdicts; code-snapshot->code-snapshot; code-fix->plans. code-demote publishes no channel and its rows are dropped.
_meta.trim_rule: Stage rows keep stageNumber/stage/channel plus the fold-read fields only: verdict rows (code-grade units + code-confirm) keep dimension/pass/severity/artifact and findings trimmed to the first finding {detail} (the anchor-nit clamp inside the blocking predicate reads findings; on this trail the clamp never decides a recorded count — every blocking verdict is pass:false severity medium, every waived one passes or sits at low/none); cite-check rows keep dimension/pass/severity; snapshot rows keep their prior fs handle; code-fix rows keep the plans fs handle + phase_count. Dropped: score/graded_at/feedback/kind/meta/ts, risk_rulings (the blocking predicate is risk-blind), verdict rows own artifacts array. Routing rows keep type/fromStage/decision verbatim. The halt row is normalized to the new kind {type:halt,stage,errMsg} with errMsg verbatim.
_meta.row_format: compact one-row-per-line JSON (each rows[] element on a single line)

findings.detail: FR2.2 asks verdict rows to carry the resolved supervisor model; the Synthesis Notes claim it ships ("FR2.2 verdict rows carry the resolved supervisor model"), and Phase 7 note 3 says "Panel should confirm Phase 2 widens SupervisorConsultResult's verdict variant with model?: string" — but Phase 2's emitted code declares no model field on any variant of SupervisorConsultResult and NO phase's changes add it. Phase 7's defensive read (result as { model?: string }).model therefore stays undefined forever, so verdict rows ship without the model while the plan's own goal-alignment sweep claims delivery. The owning edit exists nowhere.

Cross-phase API shape contradiction: Phase 1 emits rearmSupervisionState returning SupervisionRearmState directly (armedMemos items carry {id, text, target?}), pinned by Phase 1's own tests; Phase 3's emitted listener and test consume a .state wrapper (rearm.state.debounceLastMs, rearm.state.invocations, a.state.invocations) and Phase 5's memo port uses rearm.state.armedMemos plus id: memo.memoId. Phase 3's full-file emit fails tsc against Phase 1 as written, and Phase 5's port arming silently no-ops inside its onWorkflowStart catch (its arms-each-undrained-memo test fails). The implementer must pick the winning shape themselves: only Phase 5's usage is flagged (punted as grade-panel reconciles); Phase 3's and risk r5's .state spellings are unflagged.

Error-to-string idiom is inconsistent across the new supervision modules: supervision-bundle/supervision-consult use the shared toErrorMessage util (the dominant convention), supervision-sidecar defines a local errText helper, supervision-memo-port inlines an instanceof Error check, and supervision-dispatch uses String(err). Each inline form individually has precedent (paths.ts, death-scene.ts, internal-utils.ts formatError use the same inline shape), so nothing is invented, but the dominant shared-helper convention is bypassed in half the new modules. Cosmetic only — no behavioral difference.

Synthesis Notes claim FR2.2 verdict rows carry the resolved supervisor model, but no phase wires it: Phase 2's SupervisorConsultResult verdict arm (line 1692) has no model field and Phase 7 fills the row via a defensive read of result.model (line 8285) which is always undefined; Phase 7's own note 3 (line 9087) leaves the widening as an open confirmation the merge never executed, so every verdict row silently omits model, contradicting goal FR2.2 (verdict = supervisor output verbatim + model + token cost). Compiles clean and no test asserts it — a silent gap, not a typecheck catch.

FR1.6 T-noconverge silently substitutes its detection mechanism. The goal states the trigger fires when 'a fix-class stage completed but the worktree digest is unchanged from before it ran (reuse the P0/FR5 digest recipe)', but the plan's evaluator compares named-slot LENGTHS (slotLens record, evalOnRoute fires when the re-entered stage's named slot exists and its length is unchanged since the previous arrival). The semantics diverge in both directions: a stage producing different content in a same-length slot never fires (false negative vs the goal's digest check) and heavy worktree edits with an unchanged slot length do fire (divergence from 'digest unchanged'). No note, risk flag, or deferred-reason documents the substitution anywhere in the plan. The plan is otherwise fully specified, so the fix is documentation-or-restoration, not design work.

Phase 8's settle stamp (d) reads verdictRow.target with a typeof guard, but the Phase 1 SupervisionVerdictRow type declares no top-level target field, so the emitted expression fails tsc (TS2339) as written; the plan's own Notes flag this seam and the fix is a one-line drop of the first branch (memo.target is typed) or an optional-field widening — deterministic, no guessing.

Cosmetic: Phase 5 wires the supervision-memos reset into test/setup.ts via a direct relative import (../packages/rpiv-workflow/supervision-memos.js), while every existing rpiv-workflow reset in that file flows through the @juicesharp/rpiv-workflow/internal aggregator (__resetBuiltIns, __resetLifecycleRegistry, etc.); adding the reset to /internal would match the engine-package convention. Functionally identical and precedented by the relative-path resets for telemetry/i18n/voice/web-tools in the same file, so no divergence reason was strictly required.

False behavioral claim + shipped defect: the kickoff stamp is placed immediately before runSupervisorConsult with the parenthetical '(after the mode/in-flight/cap guards — state is set only when a spawn will actually happen)', but the sink's cap pre-check is FAF-only by design ('blocking consults let the consult's own authoritative cap gate decide') and tryConsumeInvocation lives INSIDE runSupervisorConsult — so a blocking consult with an exhausted cap stamps phase 'consulting', the consult returns {kind:'capped'}, and that path deliberately writes no settle stamp ('Capped and consult-in-flight-rejected hits write NO state'), stranding the running lane's dock segment on 'consulting' until run end or a later stamp — contradicting the plan's own no-strand invariant.

Phase 4's appended supervision-listener.test.ts drift describe calls registerLifecycle at module scope, but Phase 3's emitted harness hoists the mock as registerLifecycleMock — the appended block needs the one-symbol rename Phase 4's own harness-assumptions note flags before it runs as written

Goal FR1.5 explicitly requires t-drift norms 'sourced from prior runs' trail summaries', but Phase 4's supervision-drift.ts collectTokenSamples/computeDriftNorms read only prior runs' supervision sidecars via readSupervisionRows — no trail-summary source exists in the plan and no documented-deviation note covers the swap (unlike the prominently flagged FR1.2/FR1.6/FR9.2 deviations). Consequence: norms bootstrap exclusively from previously supervised runs; unsupervised trail history never contributes, delaying t-drift availability past the FRD's intent. Secondary, same unflagged status: shipped driftFactor default is 2 against the goal's recommended 3 (config-exposed).

Minor convention divergence, justified but with a misstated mechanism: models-config.ts derives raw config shapes via Static<typeof XSchema> (its ModelsConfigSchema type at models-config.ts:178), while the plan hand-writes SupervisionConfigFile in supervision-config.ts and type-imports it into the ModelsConfig interface. The stated reason (schema/resolution split) satisfies the divergence bar, but Phase 4's note that the drift sub-block is picked up automatically via Static<typeof SupervisionBlockSchema> does not hold under Phase 3's hand-written interface (no drift member is added there). Keep the raw-shape derivation consistent at the splice so the drift passthrough typechecks.

Goal FR3.2 says the supervisor child gets no write tools and Read/Grep/Glob at most, but the plan ships SUPERVISOR_TOOL_ALLOWLIST = read/grep/find/ls — ls is a fourth read-only tool beyond the goal's named set. The intent (no write tools, no repo mutation authority) is preserved and all four are read-only, but the deviation is not called out anywhere in the plan.

The appended drift-flush describe references registerLifecycle at module scope, but Phase 3's emitted harness in the same plan names the hoisted mock registerLifecycleMock — the block needs a one-line rename to run as written; the phase Notes pre-flag the harness adaptation.

Goal-demanded scope explicitly deferred: FR7.1 demands escalation 'autonomous (applied)' and the binding Direction lists four outbound ports including 'a run-scoped model override consulted at spawn'; the plan ships advisory-only escalation in P1 and defers the applied lever to P2 (risk r10, checkpoint decision, resolveModel-seam reasoning). An honest, loudly documented deferral rather than a silent drop or dishonest claim - recorded so the panel blessing stays on the record.

The emitted supervision-memo-port.test.ts import block places the @juicesharp/rpiv-config import before the @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent import, out of the Biome-sorted order every other emitted block and the live tree use; cosmetic only — the phase's own npm run check:files --write verification re-sorts it mechanically at apply time.

Phase 8 supervision-dispatch.ts Edit 4 stamp (d) reads verdictRow.target, but the Phase 1 SupervisionVerdictRow interface declares no top-level target field and Phase 7's dispatcher literal never sets one, so the emitted edit fails typecheck as written (TS2339 property target does not exist) — contradicting the phase's own 'npx tsc --noEmit exits 0' Automated Verification; the plan's note anticipates a runtime miss but the code cannot compile. Fix: drop the dead top-level branch and read only verdictRow.memo?.target (which compiles), or add an optional target to SupervisionVerdictRow in Phase 1 and set it in Phase 7 when a targeted memo is armed.
